title: Fix project.yml templating of multi-line variables
description:
A problem was identified when a variable with a multi-line value (string containing newlines) is substituted into `project.yml` via the symbolic substitution mechanism.   The newlines come in "raw" which results in multiple lines of YAML and (usually) a parsing error.   This is fixed in `nim` 3.1.1, which now
- escapes newlines (turns them into `\\n` values) by default (release 3.1.0)
- also updates the `dotenv` parser dependency to support the documented syntax for putting multi-line values in `.env` file (release 3.1.1).  Using the previous release, a multi-line value could only be specified in the process environment.  In typical use cases you will want these in the `.env` file along with other substitutions.

This PR increments the `minSandboxVersion` number to incorporate the change.

title: Add AppPlatformApp to Projects documentation
description:
This PR adds App Platform apps to the documented list of resources
supported by projects and adds an example URN for an app.

title: account: ratelimit command should not error when limit exhausted.
description: When calling `doctl account ratelimit`, we return an error if we receive a 429 from the API. This isn't helpful. The rate limit info is in the response headers. We should return them despite the 429 error so the user knows when their limit resets.

title: Unhide the sandbox and remove beta indicator
description: This PR removes the logic that hides the sandbox command when sandbox support is not installed.  It also removes the "beta" indicator from the command's help.

title: Improve friendliness of the languages table
description:
The current output of `doctl sbx status --languages` is not helpful in telling the user what keywords will actually be accepted on `doctl sbx init <path> --language <?>`.   It conflates "runtime categories" like `nodejs` with real languages (like `JavaScript`) and might also imply to some users that they need to (or even can) specify the exact release of a language runtime in the `doctl sbx init` command.

This change attempts to be clearer about the terminology and give a more helpful display.  It is designed so that the static table of languages compiled into `doctl` is inclusive of all languages for which `nim` had samples, but the actual table that is displayed is responsive to the backend reporting which runtimes are currently available.   This means that changes to the `doctl` code will not be required when (1) a new runtime is deployed for a language in the list, (2) a runtime is deprecated, (3) the default version of a runtime changes.

title: Switch from GET to POST when connecting to sandbox
description:
It has been requested by security to switch from GET to POST when connecting to the sandbox.

The portal API has already been amended to accept both for the time being so we can cut over.

This PR accomplishes the switch.   Once this is approved and merged, a new `doctl` release will be needed before support for GET can be removed from the portal API.

title: Add version info to 'sandbox status'
description:
This change allows the developer to know the version of the sandbox support, which is distinct from the doctl version.

Because `doctl sandbox status` relies on error returns for common cases (not installed, not at the right version, not connected) I decided on the following.

If you issue `doctl sandbox status` and the status is connected, you get all the information, including version:

``` 
> doctl sbx status
Connected to function namespace 'fn-5a...' on API host 'https://faas-....doserverless.co'
Sandbox version is 3.0.10-1.2.1
```

If the status is other than connected, you just get the error as before.

However, as long as sandbox support is installed, you can always get version information by specifying a flag.  The output differs according to whether your sandbox support is up to date.

```
> doctl sbx status --version
3.0.10-1.2.1
```
if up-to-date or

```
> doctl sbx status --version
Current: 3.0.9-1.2.1, required: 3.0.10-1.2.1
```
if an upgrade is required.

title: Increment nim version (improves error reporting)
description:
This change increments the included `nim` version from 3.0.8 to 3.0.10.   Benefits:

- a more comprehensible error message when a function build for `nodejs` includes an invalid `package.json` file
- the ability to see more information about remote build errors when debugging is enabled

title: Revert "Fix two small bugs (1) handling of arch=386, (2) sbx init adds unsupported config"
description: Reverts digitalocean/doctl#1153

title: Move the sandbox feature to the main branch
description:
The `feature/sandbox` has been long-lived and has been the target, to date, of all work on the `doctl sandbox` (alias `sbx`, `serverless`, `sls`) subtree.

The contents of that branch has been the source of "dev" ("beta", "pre-release") versions of `doctl` that I have been building with `goreleaser` but then uploading via manually initiated scripts to locations that have been made known to beta users.

As discussed with @andrewsomething, the purpose of doing the merge now is to work toward eliminating these special builds and releasing this feature as part of official `doctl` with some lead time prior to full support.

Note that after this PR is merged, the next release of `doctl ` will
- still have the `sandbox` tree hidden until an install step is performed
- still have the `sandbox` tree labeled as "beta" once it does become visible

Unhiding the feature and/or removing the "beta" label is not part of this PR but would presumably be done when we are ready to give full public support to the feature.

title: Fix two small bugs (1) handling of arch=386, (2) sbx init adds unsupported config
description:
This change fixes two small bugs.

1.  If the GOARCH in the `doctl` instance is 386, it is used unmodified when downloading `nodejs`.   But, `nodejs.org` uses `x86` not `386`.   Furthermore, the combination of that arch with GOOS=linux can't be supported because `nodejs` does not provide a download for that combination.  This now results in an error.
2. The command `doctl sbx init` creates a `project.yml` in which there are fields that App Platform detection for a functions component will reject.   The fix for this is in `nim` 3.0.8` which is incorporated by incrementing the `minSandboxVersion` field.

title: Make serverless and sls aliases of sandbox
description: The sole purpose of this PR is to establish serverless (and the shorter sls) as additional aliases of sandbox (and sbx).

title: Fixes to (individually) small bugs
description:
1.  There was an error in `doctl sbx upgrade` on windows due to confusion between `node` and `node.exe`.
2. There were errors during install when the temporary file area is on a different file system from the `doctl` config area.  It was using `os.Rename`.   Rather than introducing a higher overhead file move, this was changed to allocate the temporary staging area under the doctl config area so that `os.Rename` would always work.   A cleanup step was added to delete this area.
3. There were "branding" errors involving `doctl sbx watch`.   When accidentally typed without args you got a `nim` help screen.   When looking at the deployment transcript you would see a nonsensical mixture of `nim` and `doctl` syntaxes.   This was fixed partly in `doctl` and partly in the sandbox plugin (see next).
4. The `nim` and sandbox plugin versions were incremented, partly in service of the previous fix but also to pick up several useful fixes to `nim`.   See release notes: https://github.com/nimbella/nimbella-cli/releases/tag/v3.0.7

title: Fail early and cleanly when the sandbox was never connected
description:
Beta users of `doctl sandbox` have reported that a common user error is handled in a confusing way.   If the user has done `doctl sandbox install` but not `doctl sandbox connect`, and then tries other sandbox commands, the errors that come back are arbitrary and confusing because they are attempting to invoke various APIs on the serverless backend.   This change inserts a pre-check for being connected, prior to calling out to the sandbox plugin, meaning that the user always gets the informative message saying that the sandbox needs to be connected.

It is important that the pre-check not double the overhead of most calls, which is what would happen if we invoked the plugin to do the credential check.   So, the check uses a simple file existence check, which is slightly weaker since it doesn't  check for possible corruption of the credentials (etc).  The deeper check is done when `sandbox status` is called.

This PR also includes a small change to sandbox plugin DEBUG support.  It had become incomplete due to an earlier refactoring.

title: Store API host with different final domain segment
description:
This change is in support of an upcoming change to serverless clusters whereby they will have two domain names.   The API call to retrieve the sandbox namespace will, by convention, only have one of these names.  We will need to map it, conditionally, to the other.   The prefix of the namespace name ("fn-" or not) is consulted to decide whether the remapping should occur.

All fn* namespaces should be mapped to the cloudflare managed domain - doserverless.co

All other namespaces continue to be mapped to doserverless.io

This is to ensure backward compatibility for existing sandbox namespaces.

title: Support e2e tests with added env vars
description:
To support the new e2e tests for sandbox functionality (running under `bats` in the companion `doctl-sandbox-plugin` repo), it will often be necessary to manipulate the `minSandboxVersion` variable so that it can be the next (rather than current) version that is tested.    For clean tests that are not contaminated by (and do not contaminate) any existing installation, we also need to relocate the sandbox installation area for the test.   This is especially important when we add e2e tests for install and upgrade.

This PR simply adds support for two new environment variables, `minSandboxVersion`, and `sandboxDirectory` to be used for this purpose.   These will not be documented for production use by customers.

title: go 1.18
description: This updates doctl to use 1.18 and updates the test matrix

title: Increment to nim version 3.0.4 to obtain better remote build behavior
description:
The newer 'nim' invokes newer configurations of the builder system functions, allowing more efficient and secure remote builds.

Also includes a change so that builds of `golang` sandbox projects are remote by default.

title: Fix potential loop in `apps update --wait`
description:
- f11ab090 **Fix potential loop in `apps update --wait`**

  When there are no changes to make, it's possible for there to never be
  an `InProgressDeployment` returned from the API – this is more likely
  still when the `InProgressDeployment` from the `update` API is ignored,
  and later fetched via `Get` (as is currently the case).
  
  This fix assumes that `update` will return an `InProgressDeployment` if
  there is one (e.g. if it's not a no-op), so if `InProgressDeployment` is
  `nil` it treats this as a successful deployment.
  
  Fixes #1142.

title: `apps update --wait` may hang forever when the deployment is a no-op
description:
Hi,

I'm trying to use `doctl apps update --wait` in a continuous deployment pipeline. Sometimes this works fine, other times the command hangs until max attempts. Looking at the source, I think I can see the problem.

https://github.com/digitalocean/doctl/blob/62602dba745d478962fa029f2d2a2c61bb4f93e0/commands/apps.go#L352-L355

This is where the `wait` flag is applied. `waitForActiveDeployment` is called with an empty string as the deployment ID.

https://github.com/digitalocean/doctl/blob/62602dba745d478962fa029f2d2a2c61bb4f93e0/commands/apps.go#L452-L460

Inside `waitForActiveDeployment`, if the deployment ID is empty the app is fetched and `deploymentID` is set from the `InProgressDeployment` **if it's non-nil**.

However, what I can see if I hit the `update` command a few times is that sometimes `in_progress_deployment` isn't set right after updating, presumably when there are no changes to make. When this is the case, `update --wait` will loop for `maxAttempts` since `deploymentID` will remain `""` and `app.InProgressDeployment.ID` will remain `nil`.

I'm not too sure of the semantics of the DO API, but the response doesn't seem to include anything that could strictly correlate to the update. If the `update` response could be assumed to contain the `InProgressDeployment` if it's not a no-op, then it might work to only call `waitForActiveDeployment` if `app.InProgressDeployment != nil`, and pass long the `DeploymentID` otherwise.

title: Improvements to error output display
description:
Improves the output from deploy so that there is more context for the actual error.  Also ensures that a non-zero exit code is posted on a deploy error.

The change requires a change in `nim` and in the sandbox plugin code so the minimum required version is incremented in addition to the other required changes.

title: Additional testing of credential handling.
Maintain sandbox credentials on per-DO-token basis
description:
When `doctl sandbox connect` is executed, the sandbox credentials are returned and stored for a specific account or team identified by the DO API token used for the call.   But, `doctl` anticipates the use of multiple DO API tokens on a given machine, generally stored in the form of (locally) named "contexts" but also directly specifiable on the command line.  The previous practice of storing the returned sandbox credentials in a single place is thus inappropriate.   This change allows for multiple credential sets to be stored, identified by a short prefix of the token that is in use at the time of connection.   This change then allows for correct semantics when `doctl auth switch` is used or any of the `--context`, `--config` or `--access-token` flags appear on a sandbox command, altering the effective identity of the requestor.

When the sandbox was connected under one identity and the user switches to another identity for which the sandbox was not previously connected, the sandbox becomes disconnected.   This is by design.  It allows the user to do a fresh connect under the new identity.   In general this will connect to a different sandbox.

Note that the underlying Nimbella CLI is capable of storing credentials for multiple namespaces.   I did not want to load the present requirement onto that capability because in the future we are likely to allow multiple namespaces to be used within a single "sandbox."   The current change is simply maintaining the invariant that different tokens imply different identities and hence different resource sets.

title: tags: Support applying and removing tags from resources.
description:
Somehow we've never added support for tagging arbitrary resources. There is a `doctl compute droplet tag` command that allows you to tag a single Droplet, but there is no wider support for other resources or tagging multiple in one request. The PR adds new `doctl compute tag apply` and `doctl compute tag remove` commands. 

These can tag multiple resources using their URNs (e.g. `--resource do:droplet:123456 --resource do:kubernets:aaa-bbb-ccc`). The API itself does not use URNs, but it seemed like an natural approach here as we already use this pattern for other commands like assigning resources to project. So this also adds a small utility package for working with URNs.

title: Update vendored godo to v1.77.0 for apps protos updates
Improvements to flag handling and include/exclude for 'web'
description:
This PR addresses two known specific problems with flag handling and changes the strategy for "flag substitution" when calling `nim` to be less confusing and fragile.

1.  Previously, if the developer had a package called `web` and attempted to control its deployment with `--include` or `--exclude`, the results would be incorrect because `web` has special meaning to `nim`.
2. Previously, the `sandbox functions invoke` command `--param` flag required KEY and VALUE to be blank separated, which, in the context of cobra string parsing required quoting.   We now support (require) a colon separator consistent with other syntax decisions in `doctl`.  Also, the value is a string slice now, and generalizes to specifying multiple KEY:VALUE pairs.
3. In conjunction with the specific problems, but generalizing from them, the code in the `getFlagArgsArray` function has been cleaned up so that there is no longer special case processing of particular flags there.   This was fragile because it assumed it knew the meaning of these flags (which, in the long run, might fail if other commands used the same flags with a different meaning).  It was also confusing and likely to grow over time and become more confusing.   The new strategy is, in most cases, for the individual commands to fix up their flags to meet `nim` assumptions by manipulating the `CmdConfig` state prior to calling `getFlatArgsArray`.   For `invoke --param`, this won't quite work because of the many-for-one substitution at the level of tokens.  So, in that case, the command appends to the result of `getFlatArgsArray` after calling it.

title: Adopt nim 2.3.9, which fixes two bugs
description:
The Nimbella CLI version 2.3.9 contains two fixes relevant to doctl sbx commands.

1.  The use of initial './' sequences in .include file entries was causing incorrect behavior. Although unnecessary, these sequences should be harmless.
2.  Incremental deploy (used by 'doctl sbx watch') was not detecting environment changes. If the change was made to project.yml or to a contained .env file the watcher would "fire" as per the spec. However, when calculating whether actions had changed it failed to include the environment clause and the affected actions would be unchanged.

title: Increment the 'nim' version to 2.3.9
description:
The Nimbella CLI version 2.3.9 contains two fixes relevant to `doctl sbx` commands.

1. The use of initial './' sequences in .include file entries was causing incorrect behavior.   Although unnecessary, these sequences should be harmless.
2. Incremental deploy (used by 'doctl sbx watch') was not detecting environment changes.   If the change was made to `project.yml` or to a contained `.env` file the watcher would "fire" as per the spec.   However, when calculating whether actions had changed it failed to include the `environment` clause and the affected actions would be unchanged.

title: Reject 'doctl sbx init --language' value if the backend has no runtime for it.
description:
Previously, a language would be accepted if it was in a static list of languages for which we know how to generate samples.  But, not all languages in that list necessarily have runtimes in the backend, which was leading to a situation where the developer could initialize a local sandbox area that could not be deployed.

Most of the change is in `nim`, hence the required minimum version of the sandbox is incremented.

But, help texts had to change because we can no longer enumerate the supported languages in the usage help for the `--language` flag.   Contacting the controller is an asynchronous operation, and we don't want to unduly delay or hang usage help (also a bit unclear how to shoe-horn such an operation into `cobra`).    The `nim` solution refers the developer to the separate `nim info --runtimes` command.   We did not have an import of that into `doctl` so I added it but called it `doctl sbx status --languages`.   The `doctl sbx init` help is then augmented appropriately.

The check for. a runtime is omitted if you issue `doctl sbx init` before `doctl sbx connect` because, in that case, we don't have an API host to interrogate.   The language selection is just accepted as before.   Arguably, we should refuse to perform `init` until after `connect`.   But, once the namespace APIs settle down into their final configuration and we are able to do the connect operation by default at install time, the unconnected state should rarely arise and the special rule would no longer be needed.

title: Add an 'undeploy' command
description:
We deliberately omitted CRUD operations in the `functions` subtree and omitted the `packages` subtree entirely.  This was to avoid confusion between the portion of the sandbox in the local filesystem and the portion in the cloud, and maintain the idea that you push the former to the latter with `deploy`.   As this leaves developers with no way to delete resources from the namespace, we need an `undeploy`.   Given that this is a destructive operation, I made an `--all` flag obligatory when you wish to undeploy everything, and allowed specific resources to be listed on the command line.

```
Usage:
  doctl sandbox undeploy [<package|function>...] [flags]

Flags:
      --all        remove all packages and functions
```
This PR will remain a draft until I have added supporting unit tests.

title: Correct behavior for 'sandbox actv logs --poll'
description:
This change eliminates a bug in `doctl sandbox activation logs`.   The command was not behaving correctly when one of the flags `--poll`, `--tail`, or `--watch` was specified (these are actually equivalent). 

With these flags set, the command will now keep running, streaming its output to the console, making it appropriate to run in a separate window as designed.

To make this change, I changed the protocol between `doctl` and the sandbox plugin so that the plugin doesn't independently decide when the capture of output should be suppressed.   Rather, `doctl` directs this behavior with a prefixed command.

This in turn required incrementing the minimum required version of the sandbox.  The required version has been staged and will be available to `doctl sandbox upgrade`.

title: Fix lint errors in new sources on feature/sandbox
description:
In the review of the recent PR #1111, it was pointed out that my additions to `do/sandbox.go` violated `golint` rules.  After fixing those violations, `golint` was running clean on the `do` folder but still failing for `commands`.   @andrewsomething mentioned that existing code was not always lint-conformant but that new code should be if possible.

This PR fixes lint errors for those files introduced by the sandbox effort on the `feature/sandbox` branch.   I did not address failures in older source files.

title: Fix doctl sandbox connect and support additional options
description:
This change restores functionality to `doctl sandbox connect` that was lost due to changes in the functions cloud.   It uses DigitalOcean APIs to retrieve the necessary information that used to be retrieved by invoking administrative functions.   It also expands the functionality of the command as follows.
```
Usage:
  doctl sandbox connect [<token>|<namespace>] [flags]
```
The argument is now optional.  If it is omitted, the function namespaces of the account are searched to find an eligible sandbox namespace.  If it is provided, it can now be either a namespace name, or a JWT issued by the UI for the namespace (previously only a JWT was accepted).

title: Versioning and update for 'doctl sandbox'
description:
This change works in conjunction with a change to the sandbox plugin.  

The sandbox plugin build has been changed to
1.  Include a `version` file in the download.  This file becomes part of the installed sandbox support.
2. Label downloads by encoding the version in the name of the tarball to download.

By convention, version strings encode the Nimbella CLI version followed by the sandbox plugin "shim" version. 

There is an exemplar of this change already out there that can be use to test the present change.   It is at version 2.3.1-1.0.0.

The present change

1.  Adds a constant in `sandbox.go` representing the minimum version of the plugin that this `doctl sandbox` can run with.
2. Generalizes functions that determined if the sandbox is installed, so that they also detect if the sandbox is not up to date.
3. Provides a new error return and a new status in `doctl sandbox status` that expresses that the sandbox is installed but is not up to date.
4. Implements a new subcommand `doctl sandbox upgrade` which installs the "matching" sandbox version.   It shares code with `doctl sandbox install` but takes care to preserve existing credential information and also will preserve `node` if it is at the right version, to avoid using too much download bandwidth.

I have added unit tests for some of the user facing logic in `doctl sandbox [ install | upgrade ]` but these tests don't cover the core operations, which are file-system intensive.   My testing of the actual behavior, thus, was mostly manual.

I would like to merge this and leave. two follow-on items for later.
1.  Adding unit tests for the core install/upgrade operations.   I think some of this will become easier once we re-do some of that logic to stop using `tar` and start using go-native packages instead (definitely not in scope for this PR).   The refactoring to eliminate `tar` can also shift some of the internal interfaces so that more of them can use streams instead of file names and be capable of mocking.
2. Considering whether `doctl sandbox upgrade` should have an option to search for and use the latest version of the sandbox plugin instead of just one that is adequate for the current `doctl`.

title: Add sandbox command
description:
This contribution adds the command `doctl sandbox` with various subcommands:

```
doctl sandbox connect
doctl sandbox deploy
doctl sandbox get-metadata
doctl sandbox init
doctl sandbox install
doctl sandbox status
doctl sandbox uninstall
doctl sandbox watch
doctl sandbox activations get
doctl sandbox activations list
doctl sandbox activations logs
doctl sandbox activations result
doctl sandbox functions get
doctl sandbox functions invoke
doctl sandbox functions list
```

The purpose is to support local development of functions intended for deployment to App Platform when functions components are available there.

The `doctl sandbox` command is hidden unless additional software is installed dynamically.   The development of that software is beyond the scope of this PR.

Further changes (future PRs) will be needed to establish versioning and update, and probably a testing strategy.

title: Update scripts/version.sh to output desired snap version.
description:
This adds a new `--snap` flag to `scripts/version.sh` that is aware if it is being run from a tag and outputs desired snap version. I've added this as a new function to ensure that I don't unintentionally change any other usages of this script.

From a non-tagged version, `+git${SHA}` should be appended to the version. Eg.

```
 ./scripts/version.sh --snap
v1.70.0+git2cdebf6f
```
From a tagged version, it should print tag:

```
 ./scripts/version.sh --snap
v1.70.0
```

title: fixed the instructions for auto-completions on zsh
description:
The README instructions for auto-completions on Linux for zsh don't currently work.

Cobra handles zsh completion generations differently so sourcing them is not enough to activate the completions: https://github.com/spf13/cobra/blob/master/shell_completions.md#zsh-completions

Either `compdef _doctl doctl` needs to be added after sourcing, or the generated completions need to be added to a file on the $fpath.

The help message for doctl completion zsh actually has the correct instructions:

```
❯ doctl completion zsh --help

Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

$ echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

To load completions for every new session, execute once:
# Linux:
$ doctl completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_doctl"
# macOS:
$ doctl completion zsh > /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/_doctl

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.
```

This likely hasn't been an issue since there would need to be 3+ pages (at least 401 results) to be observed.

title: go.mod: remove uneeded replace
description:
`go mod why -m github.com/strechr/objx` reveals that this package doesn't
actually get built or included in the doctl command. 

```
# github.com/strechr/objx
(main module does not need module github.com/strechr/objx)
```


This replace was added to force the objx package to v0.2.0 because of security vuln from issue: https://github.com/digitalocean/doctl/issues/735

 `go list -mod=mod -m github.com/stretchr/objx` reveals that v0.2.0 is the resolved version that would be used anyway even if the package import graph included it in a build of doctl in the future.

Removing this replace statement also enables building of doctl via the new `go install pkg@version` command which won't build replace statements. This command is available in go 1.16.

To make this change I deleted the replace. Then I ran `go mod vendor` and then `go mod tidy`.

title: whitesource: set vulnerableCheckRunConclusionLevel to success
description:
Whitesource consitently reports false positives for Kubernetes related libraries.
It does not understand its versioning scheme and has some issues with Go mod's
dependency handling in geneneral. For example, it is currently reporting vulnerablities
for kubernetes-1.15.1-beta.0 while we have k8s.io/client-go v0.20.0. It does not
know that:

> For each v1.x.y Kubernetes release, the major version (first digit) would remain 0.

https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go#versioning

See for example: #843, #812. and #811

This causes confusion in PR reviews and leads to alert fatigue.

Setting vulnerableCheckRunConclusionLevel to success means:

> the conclusion status of a WhiteSource Security Check will always be
> 'Success', even if the check fails.

https://whitesource.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/WD/pages/556007950/WhiteSource+Bolt+for+GitHub#WhiteSourceBoltforGitHub-vulnerableCheckRunConclusionLevel

WhiteSource will continue to open new issues when it finds a _new_
vulnerablity, but it will no longer cause every PR to have a failed
check for things we've already determined are false positives. I think
this is a good trade off.

This PR adds a new helper method, `ensureOneArg`, that returns a `MissingArgsErr` if no args are passed or a `TooManyArgsErr` (introduced in https://github.com/digitalocean/doctl/pull/902) if more than one is passed. This allows for clearer messaging:

registry: implement garbage collection subcommands
description:
In support of the new garbage collection feature for DOCR I am introducing the following new subcommands:

* `doctl registry garbage-collection start [<registry-name>]`
  * initiate garbage collection on a registry
  * will fail if a garbage collection has already been started
* `doctl registry garbage-collection get-active [<registry-name>]`
  * returns information about the currently-active garbage collection for a registry
* `doctl registry garbage-collection list [<registry-name>]`
  * lists all garbage collections that have been requested for a registry
* `doctl registry garbage-collection cancel [<registry-name>] <gc-uuid>`
  * cancels the specified garbage collection
  * requires an explicit gc to be specified to avoid accidentally cancelling the wrong garbage collection; unlikely currently, but may become an issue in the future when we support multiple registries.

I am opening this PR before finishing the tests so as to provide an opportunity as early as possible for reviewers to provide feedback while I work on the tests.

title: Simplify Docker build process and collapse on one file.
description:
This PR aims to simplify Docker build process by collapsing it on one file. To do so, I first needed to allow overriding `GOARCH` in the Makefile.

A few things to note:

- This incorporates @BobyMCbobs' suggestion in https://github.com/digitalocean/doctl/pull/855 to run as a non-root user
- This deprecated `make native` in favor of `make build`. It was never truly native (just amd64 or 386), and as it now supports being overridden it makes less sense.
- In `make docker_build`, I copy out the resulting binary with `/bin/cp` instead of rsync to remove the unneeded dependency.

A few things to verify:

    docker build . -t doctl # Build Docker with defaults
    docker build --build-arg GOARCH=386 . -t doctl # Build Docker overriding arch
    
    make docker_build # Builds Docker w/ defaults, copies binary to builds/
    make docker_build GOARCH=arm64 # Builds Docker overriding arch, `file builds/doctl` shows aarch64 binary
    
    make build # Build binary with defaults
    make native # Still works but prints deprecation warning
    make build GOARCH=arm64 # Build binary overriding arch

description:
This adds two commands:

1. `doctl apps spec get <app-id>` prints an app spec as YAML (default) or JSON

    * I added this because `doctl apps get <app id> -o json | jq .[0].spec` is not very convenient plus it requires `jq` or similar to be installed
